sandbox-safety-policy.title: apply_patch containment check ignores the Update move-destination path
sandbox-safety-policy.rustEvidence: core/src/safety.rs:179-188 is_write_patch_constrained_to_writable_paths checks BOTH the update target AND the move destination: `ApplyPatchFileChange::Update { move_path, .. } => { if !is_path_writable(path) { return false; } if let Some(dest) = move_path && !is_path_writable(dest) { return false; } }`. A rename into a path outside any writable root makes the whole patch unconstrained (-> AskUser / Reject).
sandbox-safety-policy.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1174 calls patchWithinWritableRoots(args) which (SessionEngine.swift ~`func patchWithinWritableRoots`) iterates `files` and only tests `f.path` against the writable roots; it never tests `f.movePath`, even though PatchedFile carries movePath (Sources/Tools/ApplyPatch.swift:39,251). A `*** Update File: a.txt` with `*** Move to: /etc/evil` is judged within=true.
sandbox-safety-policy.description: Upstream treats a patch as constrained only if every Add/Delete/Update target AND every Update move destination resolves inside a writable root. The Swift live path (decidePatch consumes `within`) omits the move-destination check, so a rename whose destination is outside the writable roots is mis-classified as in-root and is auto-approved/sandboxed instead of prompting (OnRequest/Granular) or rejecting (Never). On macOS the kernel Seatbelt profile still blocks the write, but under danger-full-access (no kernel sandbox) or any unsandboxed path the wrong approval decision lets the model rename a file out of the workspace without a prompt.
sandbox-safety-policy.fixRecommendation: In SessionEngine.patchWithinWritableRoots, after checking f.path also resolve and check f.movePath (when non-nil) against the same writable roots, returning false if the destination is outside. Mirror the Update arm of is_write_patch_constrained_to_writable_paths (safety.rs:179-188). Alternatively, route the apply_patch gate through the already-correct assessPatchSafety helper (Tools/Safety.swift:158-181) which handles move_path.

config.title: config/read includeLayers emits a duplicate empty user layer when no profile-v2 is selected

When no profile-v2 is selected this is `.user(file: userFile, profile: nil)` with empty `values`, i.e. byte-identical `name` to the base `toml` layer (Config.swift:1290-1291). RequestRouter.swift:2066-2092 emits every layer with a non-nil source (including empty ones), so config/read?includeLayers=true returns TWO `{type:"user", file:<userFile>, profile:null}` entries — one with the real config, one with `config:{}` (version = sha256 of `{}`). config.description: In the overwhelmingly common case (no profile-v2 selected), Swift's `config/read` with `includeLayers=true` returns a spurious extra user layer with empty config and an identical `name` to the real user layer. Upstream emits a single user layer. A frontend that iterates `layers` (e.g. to render the layer stack or find the user layer by `name`) sees a phantom layer / two matches. `merged`/`origins` are unaffected because the empty layer contributes nothing; the divergence is isolated to the `layers` array.
config.fixRecommendation: In Config.swift `load()`, only append the `profile-v2` ConfigLayer when a profile-v2 is actually selected AND its file differs from the base user file (mirror upstream's `if active_user_file != base_user_file`). Concretely: guard the `ConfigLayer(name: "profile-v2", ...)` push behind `if let profileV2Name, !profileV2Values.isEmpty || <file != userFile>`; otherwise omit it entirely so the layer stack has a single user layer.

apply-patch.title: *** Move to: marker matched against trimmed line instead of raw line
apply-patch.rustEvidence: parser.rs:317-319 — move_path = remaining_lines.first().and_then(|x| x.strip_prefix(MOVE_TO_MARKER)); the prefix is tested against the RAW line x (no trim), unlike the hunk headers which are tested against first_line.trim() (parser.rs:287). An indented '  *** Move to: foo' therefore does NOT match as a move; it falls into the chunk loop where remaining_lines[0].starts_with('*') (parser.rs:334) is also tested on the RAW line, so '  *** Move to:' (leading spaces) does not start with '*' and is absorbed as a context line.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:518-523 — `let mt = body[i].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces); if let mp = Self.afterPrefix(mt, "*** Move to: ")`. Swift TRIMS before matching, so an indented Move-to line is treated as a rename and consumed, whereas upstream treats it as a context line.
apply-patch.description: For a leading-whitespace `*** Move to:` line, Swift recognises a move while upstream does not (it treats the line as update context). Diverging parse result for indented move markers. Models normally emit unindented markers, so traffic impact is negligible.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: In ApplyPatch.swift:518-519 test the move prefix against the RAW line `body[i]` (matching upstream's un-trimmed strip_prefix), e.g. `if let mp = Self.afterPrefix(body[i], "*** Move to: ")`, to reproduce upstream exactly. (Note this also affects the `*** End of File` / chunk `*` break which Swift already correctly tests on the raw line at 539.)

apply-patch.title: Repeated *** Update File: for the same path is merged (chunks combined) instead of treated as independent updates
apply-patch.rustEvidence: parser.rs:314-365 produces one Hunk::UpdateFile per `*** Update File:` block (no merging by path). On the production verify path verify_apply_patch_args (invocation.rs:177-227) stores them in a HashMap keyed by path, so a second update for the same path OVERWRITES the first, and each unified_diff_from_chunks is computed independently against the ORIGINAL on-disk content. On the CLI/runtime apply path apply_hunks_to_files (lib.rs:393-547) each UpdateFile hunk is applied separately, re-reading the file each time.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:469-470,556-564 — `updateIndexByPath` merges all chunks for a repeated path into a single ParsedFile (`files[idx].chunks.append(contentsOf: sectionChunks)`), then deriveNewContents applies the combined chunks sequentially against one read of the file.
apply-patch.description: Two `*** Update File:` blocks for the same path produce different results: Swift applies the merged chunks against the evolving content of a single read; upstream verify-path keeps only the last block's result (both computed against original content) while the CLI/runtime path applies each block against a fresh read. This is a rare input shape.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Do not merge by path in parseInternal; emit a separate ParsedFile per `*** Update File:` block and, in apply(), process them sequentially each re-reading the (possibly already-written) target, matching upstream apply_hunks_to_files. If matching the verify-path semantics instead, keep only the last block per path. Given the rarity, document the chosen behavior if left as-is.

apply-patch.title: Empty-but-well-formed patch errors at parse time with a parse-error message instead of the apply-time 'No files were modified.' text
apply-patch.rustEvidence: parser.rs:623-632 (test_parse_patch) — `*** Begin Patch\n*** End Patch` parses to Ok with `hunks: Vec::new()` (NO parse error). The 'No files were modified.' text is an anyhow::bail! in apply_hunks_to_files (lib.rs:371-373) surfaced via apply_hunks's stderr writeln (lib.rs:336) as a runtime tool output (exit_code 1, bare message), NOT as a parse error.
apply-patch.swiftStatus: ApplyPatch.swift:580-584 — parseInternal throws `ApplyPatchError.malformed("No files were modified.")` for an empty file list, so `parse()` throws and `apply()` surfaces it through the catch as `"apply_patch verification failed: invalid patch: No files were modified."` (ToolRouter.swift:669).
apply-patch.description: For an empty (but boundary-valid) patch, Swift `parse()` throws (upstream returns Ok with empty hunks) and the model-facing message becomes `apply_patch verification failed: invalid patch: No files were modified.` whereas upstream surfaces a bare `No files were modified.` runtime output without the `verification failed: invalid patch:` prefix. Models essentially never emit empty patches.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Move the empty-files check out of parseInternal so `parse()` can return an empty list like upstream, and have `apply()` emit the bare `No files were modified.` text (not prefixed by `invalid patch:`/`verification failed:`) when no files are present, matching the runtime stderr path. Low priority given the edge nature.

apply-patch.rustEvidence:
lib.rs:851-866 print_summary uses writeln! for the header and EACH file line, so the produced stdout ends with a trailing '
' (e.g. "Success. Updated the following files:

apply-patch.fixRecommendation: Append a trailing newline to the joined summary in ToolRouter.swift (e.g. `output: lines.joined(separator: "\n") + "\n"`) to match upstream print_summary's writeln-per-line output.

persistence-rollout.title: conversationSummary updatedAt uses seconds precision where upstream uses milliseconds
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: rollout/src/recorder.rs:1692-1693 thread_item_from_state_metadata: created_at uses to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Secs, true) but updated_at uses to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Millis, true) — distinct precision per field.
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/Persistence/ThreadStore.swift:640-641 and :649-651: both timestamp (createdAt) and updatedAt are formatted via iso8601Seconds(...) which uses a default ISO8601DateFormatter (seconds precision). updatedAt therefore loses upstream's millisecond precision.
persistence-rollout.description: Upstream emits the thread-list/summary updated_at with millisecond fractional-second precision while created_at uses whole seconds; the Swift port formats both at seconds precision, so updatedAt diverges from upstream's millisecond shape. This is an internal ConversationSummaryState field surfaced via the listing/registry wire path, so impact is cosmetic (a frontend comparing exact upstream-vs-Swift updated_at strings would see SSZ vs SSS.mmmZ), not a parse-breaking change.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: In ThreadStore.swift add an iso8601Millis helper (ISO8601DateFormatter with .withFractionalSeconds) and use it for the updatedAt field of ConversationSummaryState (keep iso8601Seconds for timestamp/createdAt), matching recorder.rs:1692-1693.

mcp.title: stdio elicitation/create routed to an arbitrary handler, not the request that triggered it
mcp.rustEvidence: codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/elicitation_client_service.rs:50-61 — create_elicitation receives the specific RequestContext (id, meta) for the in-flight call and invokes the single send_elicitation closure tied to that server; the elicitation is correlated to the originating request context, not picked arbitrarily.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpClient.swift:1015-1017 — handleServerRequest picks `activeElicitationHandlers.values.first`, i.e. an arbitrary pending handler. With multiple concurrent tool calls on the same stdio client (each registering its own handler), an inbound elicitation/create could be answered by the wrong call's handler.
mcp.description: When two tool calls are in flight on one stdio MCP client and the server issues elicitation/create, Swift resolves it via the first handler in an unordered dictionary rather than the handler belonging to the call that prompted the elicitation. In practice all handlers are the same closure today, so the observable impact is low, but it is a latent correctness gap if per-call handlers diverge.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In McpClient.swift, associate the active elicitation handler with the in-flight request id (or carry a server-supplied correlation), and when an inbound elicitation/create arrives pick the handler for the currently-blocked tool call rather than `.values.first`.

mcp.title: notifications/cancelled with a string requestId is silently dropped
mcp.rustEvidence: rmcp-0.15.0/src/model.rs:636-642 — CancelledNotificationParam.request_id is a RequestId (NumberOrString), so the wire value may be a JSON string; logging_client_handler.rs:49-58 logs it regardless of variant.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/MCP/McpNotificationSink.swift:143-148 — the decoder only reads `.number` for `requestId` (`if case .number(let n)? = paramsObject["requestId"]`); a string id yields requestId=nil and the cancellation is decoded with no id, so neither the sink nor the pending-request abort logic (McpClient.swift:945-952) can act on it.
mcp.description: Upstream tolerates a string request id on notifications/cancelled. Swift's stdio client only assigns integer ids so a string id would never match a pending request anyway, but the notification's id is still lost for diagnostics/sink consumers. Low traffic and low impact.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In McpNotificationDecoder.decode, also accept `.string` for `requestId` (store as a string variant or keep the raw value) so cancelled notifications carrying a string id are surfaced rather than nil'd out.

mcp.title: Elicitation params: progressToken not stripped from _meta before surfacing to frontend
mcp.rustEvidence: codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/elicitation_client_service.rs:110-122 (restore_context_meta) — removes the `progressToken` key from the request `_meta` (MCP_PROGRESS_TOKEN_META_KEY) and only merges the remaining `_meta` entries into the elicitation surfaced to the host.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/codex-session/main.swift:433 — mcpElicitationParams passes `params["_meta"]` through verbatim with no removal of `progressToken`.
mcp.description: Upstream scrubs the transport-level `progressToken` out of the elicitation `_meta` before forwarding it to the frontend; the Swift host forwards `_meta` unmodified, so a `progressToken` (if the server inlined one) leaks into the frontend-visible elicitation metadata. Edge-case and low impact.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In mcpElicitationParams (codex-session/main.swift), strip the `progressToken` key from the `_meta` object before constructing McpElicitationParams, mirroring restore_context_meta.

mcp.title: Elicitation form/url classification uses a heuristic instead of the `mode` discriminator
mcp.rustEvidence: codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/elicitation.rs:174-202 — the Form vs Url ElicitationRequest is selected from the actual CreateElicitationRequestParams enum variant, which rmcp tags by `mode` ("form"/"url"); url variant carries `url` + `elicitation_id`.
mcp.swiftStatus: Sources/codex-session/main.swift:427 — `let mode = params["requestedSchema"] == nil ? "url" : "form"` classifies purely by presence of requestedSchema, ignoring the authoritative `mode` tag.
mcp.description: When emitting the frontend ElicitationRequest event, Swift infers the variant from whether `requestedSchema` is present rather than the server-sent `mode` discriminator. A form elicitation that omits requestedSchema would be mislabeled as `url` (and vice versa). Note: McpElicitationPolicy.canAutoAccept (McpElicitationPolicy.swift:82-102) DOES correctly key off `mode` first, so only the surfaced event label is affected. Low impact.
mcp.fixRecommendation: In mcpElicitationParams, read `params["mode"]` first (form/url), falling back to the requestedSchema/url heuristic only when `mode` is absent — matching the policy module's own classification.

auth.title: OPENAI_API_KEY treated as an auth.json overlay; upstream load_auth never consults it
auth.rustEvidence: codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs:731-768 load_auth() consults only CODEX_API_KEY (gated by enable_codex_api_key_env, which the app-server always passes as false: app-server/src/lib.rs:470,685,775 and in_process.rs:780) and CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN (line 764, agent identity). OPENAI_API_KEY is read only by read_openai_api_key_from_env (manager.rs:469) for the request-time model client, NOT as an auth/account source.
auth.swiftStatus: Sources/Auth/AuthSupport.swift:254-262 EnvAuth.loadFromEnv builds an AuthDotJson overlay from CODEX_API_KEY > OPENAI_API_KEY > CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN; AuthManager.swift:91 always applies it as the highest-precedence source in effectiveTokens() (AuthManager.swift:311-318), ungated by any enable_codex_api_key_env flag and including OPENAI_API_KEY.
auth.description: Upstream's account/read + getAuthStatus reflect only the persisted/ephemeral store (+CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN), because the app-server builds AuthManager with enable_codex_api_key_env=false and OPENAI_API_KEY is not an auth.json source. Swift's effectiveTokens() would let OPENAI_API_KEY (or CODEX_API_KEY) shadow a real ChatGPT/persisted login and report an apiKey account. Latent in the supervisor because codexd builds AuthManager without passing env (codexd/main.swift:236-239, env defaults to [:]), but codex-session passes the full process env (codex-session/main.swift:130-154), so within a session the overlay is active and diverges from upstream's gated model.
auth.fixRecommendation: Gate the CODEX_API_KEY overlay behind an explicit enableCodexApiKeyEnv flag (default false, matching the app-server) and remove OPENAI_API_KEY from EnvAuth.loadFromEnv's auth-overlay precedence so it is only used by the model client at request time, not as an account/read or getAuthStatus auth source. Edit Sources/Auth/AuthSupport.swift loadFromEnv and AuthManager.swift effectiveTokens()/init.

auth.title: Env overlay (incl. CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN) ordered ahead of ephemeral external-ChatGPT store; upstream puts ephemeral first
auth.rustEvidence: codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs:742-768: after the gated CODEX_API_KEY check, load_auth checks the ephemeral (external ChatGPT tokens) store FIRST (lines 744-757) and only then reads CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN / agent identity from env (line 764).
auth.swiftStatus: Sources/Auth/AuthManager.swift:311-318 effectiveTokens(): the env overlay (which includes CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN via EnvAuth.loadFromEnv) is returned before the ephemeralStore is consulted, inverting the upstream precedence between CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN and host-app-injected external ChatGPT tokens.
auth.description: If both an external ChatGPT token (ephemeral) and CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN env are present, upstream prefers the external ChatGPT tokens, whereas Swift prefers the CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN agent-identity env. Low-traffic (requires both simultaneously) and latent in the supervisor (env=[:]), but a precedence inversion vs upstream.
auth.fixRecommendation: In effectiveTokens(), check the ephemeralStore before applying the CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN portion of the env overlay, mirroring load_auth's ordering (CODEX_API_KEY gated -> ephemeral -> CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN -> persistent).

auth.title: account/read derives ChatGPT email/plan from access_token when id_token lacks claims; upstream uses id_token only
auth.rustEvidence: codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs:357-388: get_account_email() reads t.id_token.email and account_plan_type() reads t.id_token.chatgpt_plan_type — both sourced exclusively from the id_token JWT claims, never the access_token.
auth.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:4192 accountJSON: `let claims = tokenClaims(tokens.idToken) ?? tokenClaims(tokens.accessToken)` falls back to decoding the access_token for email/planType when the id_token yields no claims.
auth.description: For a managed ChatGPT credential whose id_token is missing/empty but whose access_token happens to carry email/plan claims, Swift would surface a chatgpt account while upstream would treat email as absent and return invalid_request ('email and plan type are required for chatgpt authentication'). Edge-case; only differs when id_token and access_token claim sets disagree.
auth.fixRecommendation: Restrict accountJSON's claim extraction to tokens.idToken only (drop the `?? tokenClaims(tokens.accessToken)` fallback) so the MissingChatgptAccountDetails decision matches upstream's id_token-only source.

auth.title: Refresh endpoint does not honor CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE
auth.rustEvidence: codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs:930-933 refresh_token_endpoint(): reads CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE (REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE_ENV_VAR, manager.rs:96) and otherwise uses the fixed REFRESH_TOKEN_URL = https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token (manager.rs:94), independent of the configured issuer.
auth.swiftStatus: Sources/Auth/OAuthPKCE.swift:298-304 refresh() POSTs to cfg.tokenEndpoint (issuer + "/oauth/token", OAuthPKCE.swift:35). The override env var is read for revoke (Revoke.swift:122) but not for the refresh POST.
auth.description: Upstream's token refresh endpoint can be redirected to a staging/test authority via CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE independently of the issuer; Swift derives the refresh URL from the OAuthConfig issuer and ignores that env var. Primarily a staging/test-harness override, hence minor, but it is a documented non-test env var.
auth.fixRecommendation: In CurlTokenExchanger.refresh (and the URLSession variant), prefer environment CODEX_REFRESH_TOKEN_URL_OVERRIDE when non-empty before falling back to cfg.tokenEndpoint, mirroring refresh_token_endpoint().
